title: AI-Assisted Development and Managed AI Services

header.html: Use AI-assisted development tools to generate, review and optimize code (1.1.9); integrate managed AWS AI services into applications (1.1.10)
the official AWS Developer Associate (DVA-C03) exam guide, Task 1.1 (new in DVA-C03)

html:
1AI-assisted development

AI-assisted development means using AI tools inside the development workflow to write, review and improve code. The guide names these uses:

Use Example
Spec-driven code generation Write a specification first; the tool turns it into tasks and code
Intelligent code completion Suggestions while you type
Automated code review The tool flags bugs, style and risk in a change
Refactoring suggestions Cleaner structure, same behavior
Security scanning Find vulnerabilities and secrets in code

Kiro and spec-driven development

Kiro is AWS's agentic development environment. Its main ideas [Verify live]:

Concept Meaning
Specs A feature is described as requirements, design and tasks; the agent works through the tasks
Steering files Project rules (conventions, structure, standards) the agent follows every time
Hooks Automations triggered by events (for example, on file save run a check)
Exam tip

. Spec-driven = write the intent first, then generate. AI output is a draft: the developer reviews, tests and owns the result.

Good practice: review generated code, run tests, scan for security issues, never paste secrets or personal data into prompts, and keep a human in the loop for risky changes.

2Managed AI services in applications

The exam covers calling managed AI services from application code, not choosing models or designing RAG.

Service What it is for
Amazon Bedrock Managed access to foundation models through an API; no servers to run
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Services to run and operate AI agents securely (runtime, gateway, identity, memory, observability)
Amazon Quick AI-powered assistant and business intelligence for users

Calling Bedrock from code

Topic Fact
Runtime API Use the Bedrock Runtime client: InvokeModel, or the model-independent Converse API; both have streaming versions
Permission The caller's IAM role needs bedrock:InvokeModel (and streaming equivalents) on the model
Model access Access to a model must be enabled for the account [Verify live]
Errors Throttling and quota errors: retry with backoff; handle timeouts
Responses Parse the JSON body or the stream of chunks

Exam tip

. "Add a generative feature without managing infrastructure" = Amazon Bedrock called through the SDK with an IAM role. Out of scope: Polly, Rekognition, SageMaker AI, Strands Agents.

Exam tip

. The exam tests using AI tools and managed AI services, not choosing models or designing RAG. If an option is about model selection, it is out of scope.

3Exam Q&A

3.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A team writes a feature description first, then lets an AI tool produce tasks and code from it. Which approach is this?

  • ASpec-driven development
  • BBlue/green deployment
  • CTable partitioning
  • DCanary release
Show the answer

Answer: A. Spec-driven development starts from a specification.

S2Which action reflects good practice with AI-generated code?

  • AMerge it without review because AI is accurate
  • BPaste production secrets into the prompt
  • CReview it, run tests and scan it for security issues
  • DDisable all tests to save time
Show the answer

Answer: C. Generated code is a draft; the developer reviews, tests and scans it.

S3An application must add text generation without running any servers. Which service fits?

  • AAmazon EC2 with a custom model
  • BAWS Snow Family
  • CAmazon S3 Glacier
  • DAmazon Bedrock called through the SDK
Show the answer

Answer: D. Bedrock gives managed API access to foundation models.

S4A Lambda function calling Bedrock fails with an access denied error. What is the most likely fix?

  • AAdd bedrock:InvokeModel for the model to the function's execution role
  • BIncrease the function timeout to the maximum of 15 minutes
  • CAdd a dead-letter queue to the function for failed invocations
  • DEnable versioning on the S3 bucket that holds the deployment package
Show the answer

Answer: A. The caller needs permission to invoke the model.

S5Which Bedrock API is model-independent and supports multi-turn conversations?

  • APutObject
  • BConverse
  • CSendMessage
  • DGetRecords
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Converse API gives a consistent interface across models.

S6Which item describes a Kiro steering file?

  • AA deployment strategy that shifts traffic between two versions
  • BA DynamoDB index that speeds up queries on the project files
  • CA VPC endpoint that keeps the agent's traffic on the AWS network
  • DA project rule file the agent follows every time
Show the answer

Answer: D. Steering files hold conventions and standards the agent applies.

3.2 Recall questions

R1Name three AI-assisted development uses from the guide.

Show the answer

For example code generation, automated code review and security scanning.

R2What are the three parts of a Kiro spec?

Show the answer

Requirements, design and tasks.

R3What is Amazon Bedrock?

Show the answer

Managed API access to foundation models.

R4Which IAM action lets a role call a model?

Show the answer

bedrock:InvokeModel.

R5Is selecting a foundation model on the exam?

Show the answer

No, it is out of scope.

R6Who owns AI-generated code?

Show the answer

The developer, who must review and test it.

4Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
AI-assisted development spec-driven generation, completion, review, refactoring, security scanning
Kiro specs (requirements, design, tasks), steering files, hooks
Bedrock managed foundation models via InvokeModel or Converse; IAM role; backoff on throttling
Human in the loop review, test, scan; no secrets in prompts
